question.text: A horse rider covers half the distance with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> speed. The remaining part of the distance was travelled with speed <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> for half the time and with speed <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>15</mn><mo> </mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> for other half of the time. The mean speed of the rider averaged over the whole time of motion is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>7</mn></mfrac><mo> </mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is ______.

solution.text:
Let total distance travelled by horse rider be 2x.

Now, the time taken to cover first half distance is tAB=x5

Second half distance x between BC is covered in two parts, x=d1+d2

here d1 is the distance travelled with 10  m s-1 and d2 is the distance travelled with 15 m s-1 in equal time intervals t2 each.

Then, d1=10t2, d2=15t2

Second half distance x=t2(10+15)=25t2

Now, the mean speed of rider is v=2xx5+2x25=2×255+2=507  m s-1

Thus, the value of x=50.
